text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
Central Bank President Gustavo Loyola said he will present next week a new system for classifying the risk of loans above 50,000 reais granted to companies by banks.
-- CENBANK LIQUIDATES VEGA, BANFORT AND EMPRESARIAL BANKS
The Central Bank has liquidated three banks, Vega, Banfort and Empresarial, due to liquidity and other problems.
-- 91 PCT WANT PARLIAMENTARY PROBE OF VOTE BUYING SCANDAL
A poll shows 91 percent of Sao Paulo residents want a parliamentary probe (CPI) into the vote buying scandal which has rocked Brazil since Tuesday and involves Communications Minister Sergio Motta.
-- PRESIDENT SAYS FTAA IS IN NO RUSH
President Cardoso said there is no rush to establish the Free Trade Area of the Americas (FTAA), which should not represent a short-term victory for those who want immediate benefits.
-- GOVT ALLIES UNITE TO PREVENT PARLIAMENTARY PROBE

Government allies in Congress united to prevent the setting up of a parliamentary inquiry (CPI) into the vote-buying scandal involving five deputies, two governors and Communications Minister Sergio Motta.
-- CARDOSO: BRAZIL TO ACCEPT FTAA ONLY IF SOCIAL GAINS
President Cardoso said Brazil would insist on including social issues in negotiations to establish a Free Trade Area of the Americas (FTAA) which would have to benefit all citizens.
-- Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom 5521 5074151))
